subject: POC scope: vector dims, batching & reranker migration questions
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@searchly.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@retailco.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: embeddings & reranker constraints (RetailCo)

Thanks for the call today — quick summary + a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the POC. Attached: current_index_stats.csv (shard counts + avg vector size) and sample_export.jsonl.

Current setup (high level):
- Provider: legacy vector db (exported JSONL)
- Vector dim: 768 (text encoder)
- Index size: ~1.4M vectors (avg 768 dims, float32)
- QPS: ~120 peak for real-time search, bulk reindexes nightly

Questions we need your help on for the POC:
1) Recommendations for target vector dimension (256 vs 512 vs keeping 768) for 10x storage reduction while preserving quality.
2) Suggested batching for both offline indexing (fast bulk) and online upserts + real-time retrieval.
3) Normalization best practice — L2 normalize at index time or during query?
4) Reranker integration: they want to keep the learned MLP reranker but route candidate retrieval to Redis/Pinecone-style vector store. How does Redwood recommend combining reranker scores + dot-product?

We also want to understand auth options for the PoC (API key vs mTLS) and whether we can pin to dedicated capacity for predictable latency during smoke tests.

Oliver
Senior Search Engineer, Searchly

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: embeddings & reranker constraints (RetailCo)

Thanks Oliver — great context and the sample was helpful. Looping in Ben (solutions) and Priyom (embed infra) so we can give concrete guidance.

Preliminary answers:
- Dimensionality: we typically recommend 256 for retrieval-heavy workflows that value storage/cost savings; 512 if you need higher precision for semantic nuance. Given your current 768 and size, 256 is a reasonable target to test (we have model variants and quantized pipelines that keep recall high).
- Batching: offline bulk indexing: chunked batches of 10k vectors with parallel workers (we'll provide a distributed uploader script). For real-time upserts: target small batches (8-32) and use continuous batching on our SDK — aim for 16 as a starting point to balance latency/cost.
- Normalization: L2 normalize at index time and keep queries normalized too; that simplifies dot-product similarity and avoids per-query compute if you store normalized vectors.
- Reranker: recommended approach is two-stage: retrieve top-k (k=100) via dot-product, then rerank with your MLP using normalized vectors. We support returning raw scores and can add a small adapter that combines reranker logit with retrieval score (weighted sum or learned combiner).

Auth & routing notes:
- PoC: API keys are fastest to spin up; for production we support mTLS and customer-managed KMS.
- Dedicated routing: yes — we can reserve a small Dedicated pool for the POC window (2 weeks) to stabilize latency. Ben, can you confirm availability and estimate cost?

Next steps from our side:
1) We'll draft a POC scope doc with milestones (indexing, smoke tests, reranker integration), attach poc_scope.md.
2) Provide a data migration checklist for sample_export -> Redwood ingestion.
3) Fast follow call to agree on test dataset and timeline — propose 06/18 for a 30-min technical runbook session.

-Neha
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: embeddings & reranker constraints (RetailCo)

Thanks Neha — a couple clarifications and constraints from our side:

- Dim: we ran an internal down-projection experiment (768 -> 256) on a 100k sample and saw ~3% MRR drop on product search. That's acceptable if latency/cost wins are clear. We'll plan the A/B to measure impact.
- Batch sizing: nightly reindex can be parallel with worker_size=32 and batch_size=2048 per worker — we want to keep ingest time <3 hours. Online upserts: prefer 32 if you can keep tail latency <200ms.
- Normalization: we'll accept index-time L2 normalization, but note some downstream reranker expects un-normalized inputs (they apply their own scaling). We can modify the reranker to accept normalized vectors; need a short dev task.
- Reranker combine: our current combiner is score = alpha * dot + beta * MLP_score, with alpha=0.7, beta=0.3. Would you support returning raw dot and enabling us to fetch the MLP inputs?

Migration notes: sample_export.jsonl is close to what you need — currently floats in array form. We'll need a small transform to quantize to float16 if you want to reduce RAM during ingestion. Pinecone export is a simple JSONL with id/vector/metadata — should be straightforward.

Auth: API key is fine for PoC. For Dedicated smoke tests we'll want a short-term mTLS option if possible. Also, NDA is locked internally — attaching nda.pdf.

Oliver

MAP / next steps

2) Data & transform: RetailCo to share a 100k test slice (we'll accept sample_export.jsonl format). Priya — can you confirm dropoff date for the slice by EOD 06/23?
3) Ingestion & indexing: Priyom will run the ingestion using our distributed uploader and target 256-d quantized vectors for the initial run. Offline batch: worker_size=16, batch_size=4096 per worker to meet your <3h window (we'll tune).
4) Real-time config: continuous batching target=16, max_latency_ms=120. We'll monitor tail p95/p99 and adjust.
5) Reranker integration: RetailCo devs will ship an adapter to consume normalized vectors; we'll expose raw retrieval scores. Priyom — let's allocate a 2-day dev task to validate the adapter.
6) Metrics & evaluation: we'll run A/B (256 vs 512) on a holdout set and report MRR/Recall@10.
7) Tech runbook call: schedule 06/24 10:00am PT for the smoke test and demo.

Ben — please confirm Dedicated cost estimate + available start date. Priyom — once you confirm ingestion plan I'll open a short-lived Dedicated reservation for the POC. Priya / Oliver — if those dates/timelines look good, we'll circulate an updated MAP and a lightweight runbook.

Best,
